inspection_summary: All 498 logical lines were inspected. The source develops a natural-number-restricted Nyman–Beurling criterion, proves it by regularizing Möbius-weighted Beurling sums and moving norm convergence through a Fourier–Mellin isometry, and derives a quantitatively balanced finite approximant. Fourteen source-grounded units retain the distinct definitions, obstructions, analytic tools, convergence stages, corollary, smoothing alternatives, and quantitative error mechanism. Damaged formula layouts are quarantined at line level and exact symbolic transcription is not inferred.

accepted_units.title: Full and natural Beurling spans in the common Hilbert space
accepted_units.why_material: The source separates the classical span generated by all real dilation parameters from the smaller span generated only by natural parameters, making the strengthening precise relative to the classical closure criterion.
accepted_units.context_note: Keep the definitions of the fractional-part functions, χ, H, B, and Bnat together; the theorem at lines 67–69 relies on this local setup.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on function-space and dilation notation; the extracted definitions and prose are legible, while the small display at lines 43–46 should be consulted only in this checked context.

accepted_units.title: Riemann hypothesis via the natural Beurling subspace
accepted_units.why_material: The theorem replaces membership in the full Beurling span by membership in the much thinner natural-parameter span, which is the paper's central strengthening.
accepted_units.context_note: Interpret Bnat using lines 35–56; the easy reverse implication uses its inclusion in the classical span rather than a new proof mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The theorem statement is prose-supported and symbolically legible; it depends on the locally defined χ and Bnat.

accepted_units.title: Why direct natural approximants motivate regularization
accepted_units.why_material: The unsmoothed Möbius approximants have partial convergence but diverge in the ambient Hilbert space, proposed subsequences remain problematic, Selberg smoothing is an alternative, and a universal lower bound explains intrinsically slow convergence.
accepted_units.context_note: This comparison motivates using an analytic family over the full coefficient range at lines 108–137 rather than treating the first natural sum as the final approximant.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Coefficient displays have line-wrap damage, especially lines 86–94; the sequence identities, divergence claim, and lower-bound role are explicit in prose, but exact symbolic reuse requires scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Möbius-weighted analytic family as a correction of reciprocal zeta
accepted_units.why_material: Weighting natural Beurling functions by a complex exponent creates a meromorphic family tied to 1/ζ and decomposes the proof into conditional membership fε∈Bnat followed by an unconditional Hilbert-space limit fε→−χ.
accepted_units.context_note: The construction is the bridge from the approximation obstruction to the two-stage proof carried out in lines 179–310.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The display at lines 119–123 has damaged formula layout; checked prose supports the reciprocal-zeta correction and the two announced limits, not an exact normalized transcription of that display.

accepted_units.title: Zero-free half-plane controls finite Möbius Dirichlet sums
accepted_units.why_material: The quoted Balazard–Saias lemma turns a zero-free region for ζ into a uniform finite-sum approximation to 1/ζ with an explicit cutoff and vertical-growth error, enabling later norm domination.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof specializes this lemma under the Riemann hypothesis at lines 252–272 and again uses a cutoff-sensitive form in the quantitative argument.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The parameter ranges and error-term role are legible; exact typography of exponents and constants in the extracted display should be verified against the scan before symbolic reuse.

accepted_units.title: Functional equation bounds the symmetric zeta ratio
accepted_units.why_material: A ratio comparing ζ on opposite sides of the critical line is bounded by a mild vertical power independently of RH, separating an unconditional control from the conditional Möbius-sum estimate.
accepted_units.context_note: Its functional-equation reduction to a gamma ratio is later used both for dominated convergence and for removing the regularization parameter.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The half-arguments in the ratio and gamma display are typeset unevenly in extraction; the stated bound and functional-equation mechanism are prose-clear, while exact formula transcription needs scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Finite regularized natural sums and their two pointwise limits
accepted_units.why_material: Finite Möbius-weighted natural sums converge pointwise to fε, and the fundamental Möbius identity then sends fε pointwise to −χ as ε decreases, isolating the remaining task as promotion to Hilbert norm.
accepted_units.context_note: This unit supplies the candidate limits whose norm convergence is established by the transform argument in lines 211–310.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The extracted finite-sum displays are line-wrapped but the pointwise limit statements and their Möbius justification are explicit; exact term-by-term formatting should be scan-checked.

accepted_units.title: Fourier–Mellin isometry converts Hilbert norm to transform norm
accepted_units.why_material: Plancherel identifies an invertible isometry from the original L2 space to a vertical-line space, and the Mellin transform of a fractional-part function converts regularized Beurling sums into zeta times a Dirichlet polynomial.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the central representation bridge used to replace direct real-variable norm estimates with dominated convergence on the transform side.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The transform kernel and equation (2.7) are formula-dependent and have displaced fraction layout; the isometry and product structure are recoverable from checked prose, but exact normalization requires scan verification.

accepted_units.title: RH supplies transform-side domination for the finite cutoff limit
accepted_units.why_material: Littlewood convergence identifies the transform-side pointwise limit, while the conditional finite-sum estimate, the zeta-ratio bound, and Lindelöf growth combine into an integrable uniform majorant, upgrading convergence to the Hilbert norm.
accepted_units.context_note: This proves convergence first for the auxiliary weighted family Xεf2ε,n; lines 276–289 are needed to recover the unweighted natural-space membership.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The bound at lines 263–267 is extraction-damaged; the surrounding prose establishes its role as an integrable majorant, but its exact displayed factors are quarantined pending scan verification.

accepted_units.title: From weighted convergence to natural-span membership and the χ limit
accepted_units.why_material: Separate estimates on (0,1) and (1,∞) remove the auxiliary x-power, proving fε as an H-limit of finite natural sums; the identified transform limit and the unconditional ratio estimate then yield fε→−χ and complete the strengthened implication.
accepted_units.context_note: Read after the transform-side convergence of lines 243–275; it contains both the Bnat closure step and the final ε-limit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several displayed factors are tightly line-broken, but the interval split, membership conclusion, unconditional convergence claim, and final limit are stated in legible prose.

accepted_units.title: Regularized finite sums give a direct convergence criterion
accepted_units.why_material: The proof yields an RH-equivalent condition phrased as H-convergence of the finite regularized sums for every sufficiently small positive ε and is presented as avoiding the earlier Hardy-space machinery.
accepted_units.context_note: The suggested Lp extension is a proposed direction, not an established result in this source; the formal corollary is restricted to H.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The corollary is prose-stated and does not rely on a damaged display.

accepted_units.title: Subsequence sufficiency, Cesàro smoothing, and cutoff-sensitive regularization
accepted_units.why_material: The source reframes the proof as a summability method, notes that suitable subsequences in both cutoff and regularization remain sufficient, proposes Cesàro smoothing, and identifies unused cutoff dependence as the route to quantitative control.
accepted_units.context_note: The Cesàro construction is proposed for study rather than proved here; its role is methodological comparison and preparation for Proposition 3.1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The Cesàro coefficient display is legible in structure but line-wrapped; use the source-grounded smoothing description without inferring further properties.

accepted_units.title: Inverse-log-log error for an explicit natural approximant
accepted_units.why_material: Under RH the source selects a cutoff-dependent regularization scale and states a finite natural Beurling approximant whose H-distance from χ is bounded by an inverse one-third power of log log n.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof mechanism and the choice of regularization parameter occur at lines 357–430.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The approximant display at lines 342–348 has displaced exponent layout; the stated dependence, H-distance, and rate are prose-supported, while exact coefficient typography must be verified from the scan.

accepted_units.title: Balance zero-sensitive shift error against finite-sum truncation
accepted_units.why_material: Plancherel splits the approximation error into a finite Dirichlet-sum discrepancy and a shifted-zeta ratio discrepancy; zero-near and zero-far estimates give the latter an ε^(2/3) scale, a cutoff-sensitive Balazard–Saias estimate controls the former, and choosing ε proportional to 1/log log n balances the bounds.
accepted_units.context_note: This is explicitly a proof sketch under RH. It supplies the mechanism behind Proposition 3.1 rather than an unconditional approximation theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displays at lines 360–378 and 407–423 are materially layout-damaged. Adjacent prose safely supports the two-error decomposition, the stated rate scales, and the balancing choice; exact integrands, constants, and normalized exponents are quarantined and require scan verification.

v1_context_repairs.reason: The carried span starts at the theorem and omits the local definitions of H, B, Bnat, and the classical criterion needed to interpret the strengthened construction without reconstruction.

The carried proof span explicitly invokes both technical lemmas; including their statements preserves the conditional finite-sum estimate and unconditional ratio bound on which the transform domination depends.
The carried quantitative span begins after the corollary and summability discussion that introduce the cutoff-sensitive regularization and explain why the quantitative proposition is pursued.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Natural-span strengthening through regularized closure
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The strengthened criterion is obtained by proving each positive-regularization limit lies in the smaller natural span under RH, then using an unconditional vanishing-regularization limit to reach χ in that closed span.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The synthesis is specific to the source's Hilbert-space setup and cited analytic estimates; it does not establish the proposed Lp extension.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Conditional and unconditional work separate on the transform side
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Fourier–Mellin representation isolates RH-dependent convergence of Möbius Dirichlet polynomials from an RH-independent symmetric zeta-ratio bound, allowing the two nested limits to be justified by different inputs.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Exact transform normalizations and several displayed factors require scan verification; the candidate asserts only the source-explicit division of proof roles.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Approximation obstruction guides smoothing and parameter balance
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Divergence of the unsmoothed natural sums and a universal slow-rate bound motivate summability; retaining cutoff dependence then permits regularization to balance finite-sum error against zeta-shift error and yields the stated inverse-log-log rate.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The quantitative conclusion is conditional on RH, the proof is explicitly a sketch, and the formula-damaged displays must not be treated as exact transcriptions.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A hierarchy of source-internal equivalent tests
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The paper connects the natural-span closure statement to Hilbert convergence of every sufficiently small regularized finite-sum family, while pointwise Möbius cancellation alone is shown to be insufficient until norm convergence is supplied.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source states special-subsequence sufficiency only informally and does not give it a separate proved theorem in the inspected text.
